rationale.conceptual: The method is established (DFT with CHE) but non-trivial to implement correctly: requires building atomic models, selecting proper pseudopotentials, performing spin-polarized calculations, and applying zero-point energy and entropy corrections. The correctness depends on careful handling of computational parameters and free-energy referencing. Not a novel algorithm, but not a simple library call.
rationale.execution: The pipeline involves at least 6 interdependent stages: model construction, reference calculations, total energy runs, formation energy computation, adsorbate energy calculations, and overpotential evaluation. Each coordination number (5 models) requires multiple DFT relaxations and SCF runs, plus post-processing. The environment setup (Quantum ESPRESSO, pseudopotentials) is fragile and requires orchestration of many job files. This qualifies as a long pipeline with multiple handoffs.

This involves building models, running reference and intermediate adsorbate calculations, and applying the computational hydrogen electrode method. While the underlying method (Nørskov's CHE approach) is established, executing it correctly demands careful implementation of multiple DFT steps, geometry optimizations, and free-energy corrections. The pipeline comprises at least six stages with dependencies and non-trivial tooling (Quantum ESPRESSO installation, pseudopotential management).
